extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, claim drafters, patent attorneys, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on choosing and interpreting transitional phrases in patent claim drafting and examination, focusing on how phrases like 'comprising', 'consisting essentially of', and 'consisting of' define claim scope and affect prior art searching, prosecution, and litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of Transitional Phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional phrases in patent claims define the scope of a claim with respect to additional components or steps and determine whether a claim is open-ended or closed to additional elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These phrases significantly impact the breadth of patent protection and how the claim is interpreted during patent examination or litigation. Choice of transitional phrase should be made with awareness of prosecution and enforcement consequences (MPEP 2111.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprising — open-ended / inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: The transitional phrase 'comprising' is open-ended and is inclusive of additional, unrecited elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'comprising' when an open-ended claim is desired that allows the presence of additional components or steps beyond those recited. MPEP notes that 'comprising' is open-ended and inclusive of additional elements (MPEP 2111.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting of — closed to unrecited elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims using 'consisting of' are closed to unrecited elements and exclude additional components or steps not explicitly recited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'consisting of' when a closed claim scope is intended that expressly excludes any elements not recited. This limits claim breadth and can affect infringement and validity analyses (MPEP 2111.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting essentially of — limits to basic and novel characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The transitional phrase 'consisting essentially of' limits claim scope to the basic and novel characteristics of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Consisting essentially of' excludes additional elements that materially affect the basic and novel properties of the invention but permits those that do not. This phrase narrows scope relative to 'comprising' but is broader than 'consisting of' (MPEP 2111.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting essentially of — treated as comprising for prior art searching
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consisting essentially of' is equivalent to 'comprising' for purposes of prior art searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prior art search procedures, MPEP states that 'consisting essentially of' should be treated like 'comprising' (MPEP 2111.03). Practitioners should be aware that narrowing semantic differences may not change prior art considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composed of — interpreted flexibly
rubrics_metrics.description: The transitional phrase 'composed of' is interpreted flexibly rather than being rigidly open- or closed-ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP indicates 'composed of' does not have a fixed rigid meaning and must be interpreted in context; drafters should clarify intended scope in specification or choose a more precise transitional phrase if necessary (MPEP 2111.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Having — interpret based on specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'having' (or similar formulations) must be interpreted in light of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope imparted by 'having' depends on its usage and supporting disclosure in the specification; examiners and drafters should consult the specification to resolve whether 'having' is intended to be limiting (MPEP 2111.03).
